curriculum: Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 (with IM Grade 8 lessons)
source: Seattle Public Schools, Algebra 1 Sample Calendar 2026-27

sequence.district_title: Unit 0 Day 1
Unit 0 Day 2
Unit 0 Day 3
Unit 1 Check Your Readiness
Unit 1 Lesson 1: Getting to Know You
sequence.target: I can tell statistical questions from non-statistical questions and can explain the difference. I can tell the difference between numerical and categorical data.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 2: Data Representations
sequence.target: I can find the five-number summary for data. I can use a dot plot, histogram, or box plot to represent data.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 3: A Gallery of Data + Section A Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can graphically represent the data that I collected and critique the representations of others’ data.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 4: The Shape of Distributions
sequence.target: I can use a graphical representation of data to suggest a situation that produced the data pictured. I can use the terms "symmetric," "skewed," "uniform," "bimodal," and "bell-shaped" to describe the shape of a distribution.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 5: Calculating Measures of Center and Variability + Section B Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can calculate mean absolute deviation, interquartile range, mean, and median for a set of data.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 9: Technological Graphing
sequence.target: I can use technology to create graphic representations of data and calculate statistics.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 10: The Effect of Extremes
sequence.target: I can describe how an extreme value will affect the mean and median. I can use the shape of a distribution to compare the mean and median.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 11: Comparing and Contrasting Data Distributions
sequence.target: I can arrange data sets in order of variability, given graphic representations.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 12: Standard Deviation
sequence.target: I can describe standard deviation as a measure of variability. I can use technology to compute standard deviation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 13: More Standard Deviation
sequence.target: I can use standard deviation to say something about a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 14: Outliers
sequence.target: I can find values that are outliers, investigate their source, and figure out what to do with them. I can tell how an outlier affects mean, median, IQR, or standard deviation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 15: Comparing Data Sets + Section D Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can compare and contrast situations using measures of center and measures of variability.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Lesson 16: Analyzing Data
sequence.target: I can collect data from an experiment and compare the results using measures of center and measures of variability.

sequence.district_title: Unit 1 Review
Unit 1 End of Unit Assessment
Unit 2 Check Your Readiness
Unit 2 Lesson 1: Planning a Party + Lesson 2: Writing Equations to Model Relationships (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can explain the meaning of the term “constraints.” I can tell which quantities in a situation can vary and which ones cannot. I can use letters and numbers to write expressions representing the quantities in a situation. I can use letters and numbers to write equations representing the relationships in a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 3: Writing Equations to Model Relationships (Part 2)
sequence.target: I can use words and equations to describe the patterns I see in a table of values or in a set of calculations. When given a description of a situation, I can use representations like diagrams and tables to help make sense of the situation and write equations for it.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 4: Equations and Their Solutions
sequence.target: I can explain what it means for a value or pair of values to be a solution to an equation. I can find solutions to equations by reasoning about a situation or by using algebra.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 5: Equations and Their Graphs + Section A Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can use graphing technology to graph linear equations and identify solutions to the equations. I understand how the coordinates of the points on the graph of a linear equation are related to the equation. When given the graph of a linear equation, I can explain the meaning of the points on the graph in terms of the situation it represents.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 4 Lesson 3: Balanced Moves + Grade 8 Unit 4 Lesson 4: More Balanced Moves
sequence.target: I can add, subtract, multiply, or divide each side of an equation by the same expression to get a new equation with the same solution. I can make sense of multiple ways to solve an equation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 6: Equivalent Equations
sequence.target: I can tell whether two expressions are equivalent and explain why or why not. I know and can identify the moves that can be made to transform an equation into an equivalent one. I understand what it means for two equations to be equivalent, and how equivalent equations can be used to describe the same situation in different ways.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 7: Explaining Steps for Rewriting Equations
sequence.target: I can explain why some algebraic moves create equivalent equations but some do not. I know how equivalent equations are related to the steps of solving equations. I know what it means for an equation to have no solutions and can recognize such an equation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 8: Which Variable to Solve for? (Part 1) + Lesson 9: Which Variable to Solve for? (Part 2)
sequence.target: Given an equation, I can solve for a particular variable (like height, time, or length) when the equation would be more useful in that form. I know the meaning of the phrase “to solve for a variable.” I can write an equation to describe a situation that involves multiple quantities whose values are not known, and then solve the equation for a particular variable. I know how solving for a variable can be used to quickly calculate the values of that variable.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 3 Lesson 8: Translating to y=mx+b + Grade 8 Unit 3 Lesson 9: Slopes Don't Have to Be Positive
sequence.target: I can explain where to find the slope and vertical intercept in both an equation and its graph. I can write equations of lines using y=mx+b. I can create a graph of a situation that has a negative slope. I can determine if a situation or a graph has a slope that is positive, negative, or zero and explain how I know.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 3 Lesson 10: Calculating Slope
sequence.target: I can calculate positive and negative slopes given two points on the line.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 3 Lesson 12: Equations of All Kinds of Lines
sequence.target: I can write equations of lines that have a positive or a negative slope. I can write equations of vertical and horizontal lines.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 10: Connecting Equations to Graphs (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can describe the connections between an equation of the form ax+by=c, the features of its graph, and the rate of change in the situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 11: Connecting Equations to Graphs (Part 2) + Section B Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can find the slope and vertical intercept of a line with equation ax+by=c.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 4 Lesson 12: Systems of Equations
sequence.target: I can explain the solution to a system of equations in a real-world context. I can explain what a system of equations is. I can make graphs to find an ordered pair that two real-world situations have in common.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 12: Writing and Graphing Systems of Linear Equations
sequence.target: I can explain what we mean by “the solution to a system of linear equations” and can explain how the solution is represented graphically. I can explain what we mean when we refer to two equations as a system of equations. I can use tables and graphs to solve systems of equations.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 13: Solving Systems by Substitution
sequence.target: I can solve systems of equations by substituting a variable or an expression. I know more than one way to perform substitution and can decide which way or what to substitute based on how the given equations are written.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 14: Solving Systems by Elimination (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can solve systems of equations by adding or subtracting them to eliminate a variable. I know that adding or subtracting equations in a system creates a new equation, where one of the solutions to this equation is the solution to the system.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 15: Solving Systems by Elimination (Part 2)
sequence.target: I can explain why adding or subtracting two equations that share a solution results in a new equation that also shares the same solution.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 16: Solving Systems by Elimination (Part 3)
sequence.target: I can solve systems of equations by multiplying each side of one or both equations by a factor, then adding or subtracting the equations to eliminate a variable. I understand that multiplying each side of an equation by a factor creates an equivalent equation whose graph and solutions are the same as that of the original equation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 17: Systems of Linear Equations and Their Solutions
sequence.target: I can tell how many solutions a system has by graphing the equations or by analyzing the parts of the equations and considering how they affect the features of the graphs. I know the possibilities for the number of solutions a system of equations could have.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 18: Asking About Solving Systems + Section C Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can get more information about a problem in order to write and solve a system of linear equations.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Lesson 19: Linear Patterns
sequence.target: I can solve linear equations algebraically. I can write linear equations to create a pattern.

sequence.district_title: Unit 2 Review
Unit 2 End of Unit Assessment (CEA)
Unit 3 Check Your Readiness
Grade 8 Unit 6 Lesson 9: Looking for Associations
sequence.target: I can identify the same data represented in a bar graph, a segmented bar graph, and a two-way table. I can use a two-way frequency table or relative frequency table to find associations among variables.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Lesson 1: Two-way Tables + Lesson 2: Relative Frequency Tables
sequence.target: I can calculate missing values in a two-way table. I can create a two-way table for categorical data given information about a situation. I can describe what the values in a two-way table mean in the context of the situation. I can calculate values in a relative frequency table and describe what the values mean in everyday language.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Lesson 2: Relative Frequency Tables + Lesson 3: Associations in Categorical Data + Section A Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can calculate values in a relative frequency table and describe what the values mean in everyday language. I can look for patterns in two-way tables and relative frequency tables to see if there is a possible association between two variables.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 6 Lesson 3: What a Point in a Scatter Plot Means
sequence.target: I can describe the meaning of a point in a scatter plot in context.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 6 Lesson 4: Fitting a Line to Data
sequence.target: I can pick out outliers on a scatter plot. I can use a model to predict values for data.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Lesson 4: Linear Models
sequence.target: I can describe the rate of change and y-intercept for a linear model that represents a situation. I can draw a linear model that fits the data well and use the linear model to estimate values I want to find.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Lesson 5: Fitting Lines
sequence.target: I can describe the rate of change and y-intercept for a linear model that represents a situation. I can use technology to find the line of best fit.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Lesson 7: The Correlation Coefficient
sequence.target: I can describe the goodness of fit of a linear model using the correlation coefficient. I can match the correlation coefficient with a scatter plot and linear model.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Lesson 8: Using the Correlation Coefficient
sequence.target: I can describe the strength of a relationship between two variables. I can use technology to find the correlation coefficient and explain what the value tells me about a linear model that represents a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Lesson 9: Causal Relationships
sequence.target: I can look for connections between two variables to analyze whether or not there is a causal relationship.

sequence.district_title: Unit 3 Review
Unit 3 End of Unit Assessment
Unit 4 Check Your Readiness
Unit 4 Lesson 1: Representing Situations with Inequalities
sequence.target: I can write inequalities that represent the constraints in a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 2: Solutions to Inequalities in One Variable
sequence.target: I can graph the solution to an inequality in one variable. I can solve one-variable inequalities and interpret the solutions in terms of the situation. I understand that the solution to an inequality is a range of values (such as x\gt7) that makes the inequality true.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 3: Writing and Solving Inequalities in One Variable + Section A Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can analyze the structure of an inequality in one variable to help determine if the solution is greater or less than the solution to the related equation. I can write and solve inequalities to answer questions about a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 4: Graphing Linear Inequalities in Two Variables (Part 1)
sequence.target: Given a two-variable inequality and the graph of the related equation, I can determine on which side of the line the solutions to the inequality will fall. I can describe the graph that represents the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 5: Graphing Linear Inequalities in Two Variables (Part 2)
sequence.target: Given a two-variable inequality that represents a situation, I can interpret points in the coordinate plane and decide if they are solutions to the inequality. I can find the solutions to a two-variable inequality by using the graph of a related two-variable equation. I can write inequalities to describe the constraints in a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 6: Solving Problems with Inequalities in Two Variables + Section B Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can use graphing technology to find the solution to a two-variable inequality. When given inequalities, graphs, and descriptions that represent the constraints in a situation, I can connect the different representations and interpret them in terms of the situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 7: Solutions to Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
sequence.target: I can write a system of inequalities to describe a situation, find the solution by graphing, and interpret points in the solution. I know what is meant by "the solutions to a system of inequalities" and can describe the graphs that represent the solutions. When given descriptions and graphs that represent two different constraints, I can find values that satisfy each constraint individually, and values that satisfy both constraints at once.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 8: Solving Problems with Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
sequence.target: I can explain how to tell if a point on the boundary of the graph of the solutions to a system of inequalities is a solution or not.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Lesson 9: Modeling with Systems of Inequalities in Two Variables + Section C Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can interpret inequalities and graphs in a mathematical model. I know how to choose variables, specify the constraints, and write inequalities to create a mathematical model.

sequence.district_title: Unit 4 Review
Unit 4 End of Unit Assessment
Unit 5 Check Your Readiness
Grade 8 Unit 5 Lesson 2: Introduction to Functions
sequence.target: I know that a function is a rule with exactly one output for each allowable input. I know that if a rule has exactly one output for each allowable input, then the output depends on the input.

sequence.district_title: Grade 8 Unit 5 Lesson 3: Equations for Functions
sequence.target: I can find the output of a function when I know the input. I can name the independent and dependent variables for a given function and represent the function with an equation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 1: Describing and Graphing Situations
sequence.target: I can explain when a relationship between two quantities is a function. I can identify independent and dependent variables in a function and use words and graphs to represent the function. I can make sense of descriptions and graphs of functions and explain what they tell us about situations.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 2: Function Notation
sequence.target: I can use function notation to express functions that have specific inputs and outputs. I understand what function notation is and why it exists. When given a statement written in function notation, I can explain what it means in terms of a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 3: Interpreting and Using Function Notation
sequence.target: I can describe the connections between a statement in function notation and the graph of the function. I can use function notation to efficiently represent a relationship between two quantities in a situation. I can use statements in function notation to sketch a graph of a function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 4: Using Function Notation to Describe Rules (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can make sense of rules of functions when they are written in function notation, and create tables and graphs to represent the functions. I can write equations that represent the rules of functions.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 5: Using Function Notation to Describe Rules (Part 2) + Section A Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can use technology to graph a function given in function notation and use the graph to find the values of the function. I know different ways to find the value of a function and to solve equations written in function notation. I know what makes a function a linear function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 6: Features of Graphs
sequence.target: I can identify important features of graphs of functions and explain what they mean in the situations represented. I understand and can use the terms “horizontal intercept,” “vertical intercept,” “maximum,” and “minimum” when talking about functions and their graphs.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 7: Using Graphs to Find Average Rate of Change
sequence.target: I understand the meaning of the term “average rate of change.” When given a graph of a function, I can estimate or calculate the average rate of change between two points.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 8: Interpreting and Creating Graphs
sequence.target: I can explain the average rate of change of a function in terms of a situation. I can make sense of important features of a graph and explain what they mean in a situation. When given a description or a visual representation of a situation, I can sketch a graph that shows important features of the situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 9: Comparing Graphs + Section B Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can compare the features of graphs of functions and explain what they mean in the situations represented. I can make sense of an equation of the form f(x)=g(x) in terms of a situation and a graph, and know how to find the solutions.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Review
Unit 5 Mid-Unit Assessment (CEA)
Unit 5 Lesson 10: Domain and Range (Part 1)
sequence.target: I know what is meant by the “domain” and “range” of a function. When given a description of a function in a situation, I can determine a reasonable domain and range for the function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 11: Domain and Range (Part 2)
sequence.target: When given a description of a function in a situation, I can determine a reasonable domain and range for the function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 12: Piecewise Functions + Section C Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can make sense of a graph of a piecewise function in terms of a situation and sketch a graph of the function when the rules are given. I can make sense of the rules of a piecewise function when they are written in function notation and explain what they mean in the situation represented. I understand what makes a function a piecewise function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 13: Absolute Value Functions (Part 1) + Lesson 14: Absolute Value Functions(Part2)
sequence.target: Given a set of numerical guesses and a target number, I can calculate absolute errors and create a scatter plot of the data. I can analyze and describe features of a scatter plot that shows absolute error data. I can describe the general relationship between guesses and absolute errors using words or equations. I can describe the effects of adding a number to the expression that defines an absolute value function. I can explain the meaning of absolute value function in terms of distance. When given an absolute value function in words or in function notation, I can make sense of it and create a table of values and a graph to represent it.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 15: Solving Equations with Absolute Values
Unit 5 Lesson 16: Solve Inequalities with Absolute Values + Section D Checkpoint
Unit 5 Lesson 17: Inverse Functions
sequence.target: I understand the meaning of “inverse function” and how it could be found. When given a linear function that represents a situation, I can use words and equations to describe the inverse function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 19: Writing Inverse Functions to Solve Problems
sequence.target: I can write a linear function to model given data and find the inverse of the function. When given a linear function defined using function notation, I know how to find its inverse.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Lesson 20: Using Functions to Model Battery Power (can be used as the review)
sequence.target: I can write a function to describe a situation and make predictions.

sequence.district_title: Unit 5 Review
Unit 5 End of Unit Assessment
Unit 6 Check Your Readiness
Unit 6 Lesson 1: Growing and Growing
sequence.target: I can compare growth patterns using calculations and graphs.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 2: Patterns of Growth + Section A Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can use words and expressions to describe patterns in tables of values. When I have descriptions of linear and exponential relationships, I can write expressions and create tables of values to represent them.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 3: Representing Exponential Growth
sequence.target: I can explain the connections between an equation and a graph that represents exponential growth. I can write and interpret an equation that represents exponential growth.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 4: Representing Exponential Decay
sequence.target: I can explain the meanings of a and b in an equation that represents exponential decay and is written as y=a \boldcdot b^x.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 5: Understanding Decay
sequence.target: I can use only multiplication to represent "decreasing a quantity by a fraction of itself." I can write an expression or equation to represent a quantity that decays exponentially. I know the meanings of “exponential growth” and “exponential decay.”

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 6: Analyzing Graphs + Section B Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can use graphs to compare and contrast situations that involve exponential decay. I can use information from a graph to write an equation that represents exponential decay.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 7: Using Negative Exponents
sequence.target: I can describe the meaning of a negative exponent in equations that represent exponential decay. I can write and graph an equation that represents exponential decay to solve problems.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 8: Exponential Rules
Unit 6 Lesson 9: Unit Fractional Exponents + Section C Checkpoint
Unit 6 Lesson 11: Exponential Situations as Functions
sequence.target: I can use function notation to write equations that represent exponential relationships. When I see relationships in descriptions, tables, equations, or graphs, I can determine whether the relationships are functions.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 12: Interpreting Exponential Functions
sequence.target: I can analyze a situation and determine whether it makes sense to connect the points on the graph that represents the situation. When I see a graph of an exponential function, I can make sense of and describe the relationship using function notation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 13: Looking at Rates of Change
sequence.target: I can calculate the average rate of change of a function over a specified period of time. I know how the average rate of change of an exponential function differs from that of a linear function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 14: Modeling Exponential Behavior
Unit 6 Lesson 15: Reasoning about Exponential Graphs (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can describe the effect of changing a and b on a graph that represents f(x)=a \boldcdot b^x. I can use equations and graphs to compare exponential functions.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 16: Reasoning about Exponential Graphs (Part 2) + Section D Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can explain the meaning of the intersection of the graphs of two functions in terms of the situations they represent. When I know two points on a graph of an exponential function, I can write an equation for the function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Mid-Unit Assessment
Unit 6 Lesson 18: Functions Involving Percent Change
sequence.target: I can use graphs to illustrate and compare different percent increases. I can write a numerical expression or an algebraic expression to represent the result of applying a percent increase repeatedly.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 19: Compounding Interest
sequence.target: I can explain why applying a percent increase, p, n times is like or unlike applying the percent increase np.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 20: Different Compounding Intervals
sequence.target: I can calculate interest when I know the starting balance, interest rate, and compounding intervals. When given interest rates and compounding intervals, I can choose the better investment option.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 21: Expressed in Different Ways + Section E Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can solve problems using exponential expressions written in different ways. I can write equivalent expressions to represent situations that involve repeated percent increase or decrease.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 22: Which One Changes Faster?
sequence.target: I can use tables, calculations, and graphs to compare growth rates of linear and exponential functions and to predict how the quantities change eventually.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 23: Changes over Equal Intervals + Section F Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can calculate rates of change of functions given graphs, equations, or tables. I can use rates of change to describe how a linear function and an exponential function change over equal intervals.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Lesson 24: Predicting Populations
sequence.target: I can determine how well a chosen model fits the given information. I can determine whether to use a linear function or an exponential function to model real-world data.

sequence.district_title: Unit 6 Review
Unit 6 End of Unit Assessment
Unit 7 Check Your Readiness + Unit 8 Check Your Readiness
Unit 7 Lesson 1: A Different Kind of Change + Lesson 2: How Does it Change?
sequence.target: I can create drawings, tables, and graphs that represent the area of a garden. I can recognize a situation represented by a graph that increases and then decreases. I can describe how a pattern is growing. I can tell whether a pattern is growing linearly, exponentially, or quadratically. I know a quadratic expression has a squared term.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7: Section A Checkpoint + Lesson 3: Building Quadratic Functions from Geometric Patterns
sequence.target: I can explain using graphs, tables, or calculations that exponential functions eventually grow faster than do quadratic functions. I can recognize quadratic functions written in different ways. I can use information from a pattern of shapes to write a quadratic function.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 4: Comparing Quadratic and Exponential Functions
sequence.target: I can explain using graphs, tables, or calculations that exponential functions eventually grow faster than do quadratic functions.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 5: Building Quadratic Functions to Describe Situations (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can explain the meaning of the terms in a quadratic expression that represents the height of a falling object. I can use tables, graphs, and equations to represent the height of a falling object.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lessons 6 & 7: Building Quadratic Functions to Describe Situations (Part 2 &3)
sequence.target: I can create quadratic functions and graphs that represent a situation. I can relate the vertex of a graph and the zeros of a function to a situation. I know that the domain of a function can depend on the situation it represents. I can choose a domain that makes sense in a revenue situation. I can model revenue with quadratic functions and graphs. I can relate the vertex of a graph and the zeros of a function to a revenue situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7: Section B Checkpoint + Lesson 8: Equivalent Quadratic Expressions
sequence.target: I can rewrite quadratic expressions in different forms by using an area diagram or the distributive property.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 9: Standard Form and Factored Form
sequence.target: I can rewrite quadratic expressions given in factored form in standard form, using either the distributive property or a diagram. I know the difference between “factored form” and “standard form.”

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 10: Graphs of Functions in Standard and Factored Forms + Section C Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can explain the meaning of the intercepts on a graph of a quadratic function in terms of the situation it represents. I know how the numbers in the factored form of a quadratic expression relate to the intercepts of its graph.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Mid-Unit Assessment
Unit 7 Lesson 11: Graphing from the Factored Form
sequence.target: I can graph a quadratic function given in factored form. I know how to find the vertex and y-intercept of the graph of a quadratic function in factored form without graphing it first.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 12: Graphing the Standard Form (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can explain how the a and c in y=ax^2+bx+c affect the graph of the equation. I understand how graphs, tables, and equations that represent the same quadratic function are related.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 14: Graphs that Represent Situations
sequence.target: I can explain how a quadratic equation and its graph relate to a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 15: Vertex Form
sequence.target: I can recognize the “vertex form” of a quadratic equation. I can relate the numbers in the vertex form of a quadratic equation to its graph.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 16: Graphing from the Vertex Form
sequence.target: I can graph a quadratic function given in vertex form, showing a maximum or minimum and the y-intercept. I know how to find a maximum or a minimum of a quadratic function given in vertex form without first graphing it.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Lesson 17: Changing the Vertex + Section D Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can describe how changing a number in the vertex form of a quadratic function affects its graph.

sequence.district_title: Unit 7 Review
Unit 7 End of Unit Assessment (CEA)
Unit 8 Lesson 1: Finding Unknown Inputs
sequence.target: I can explain the meaning of a solution to an equation in terms of a situation. I can write a quadratic equation that represents a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 2: When and Why Do We Write Quadratic Equations?
sequence.target: I can recognize the factored form of a quadratic expression and know when it can be useful for solving problems. I can use a graph to find the solutions to a quadratic equation but also know its limitations.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8: Section A Checkpoint + Lesson 3: Solving Quadratic Equations by Reasoning
sequence.target: I can find solutions to quadratic equations by reasoning about the values that make the equation true. I know that quadratic equations may have two solutions.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 4: Solving Quadratic Equations with the Zero-Product Property
sequence.target: I can explain the meaning of the “zero product property.” I can find solutions to quadratic equations when one side is a product of factors and the other side is zero.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 5: How Many Solutions
sequence.target: I can explain why dividing by a variable to solve a quadratic equation is not a good strategy. I know that quadratic equations can have no solutions and can explain why when there are none.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 6: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can explain how the numbers in a quadratic expression in factored form relate to the numbers in an equivalent expression in standard form. When given quadratic expressions in factored form, I can rewrite them in standard form. When given quadratic expressions in the form of x^2+bx+c, I can rewrite them in factored form.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 7: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 2)
sequence.target: I can explain how the numbers and signs in a quadratic expression in factored form relate to the numbers and signs in an equivalent expression in standard form. When given a quadratic expression given in standard form with a negative constant term, I can write an equivalent expression in factored form.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 8: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 3)
sequence.target: I can explain why multiplying a sum and a difference, (x+m)(x-m), results in a quadratic expression with no linear term.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 9: Solving Quadratic Equations by Using Factored Form
sequence.target: I can rearrange a quadratic equation to be written as an expression in factored form equal to zero and find the solutions. I can recognize the number of solutions for a quadratic equation from the factored form.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 10: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 4) + Section B Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can use the factored form of a quadratic expression or a graph of a quadratic function to answer questions about a situation. When given quadratic expressions of the form ax^2+bx+c, where a is not 1, I can write equivalent expressions in factored form.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Mid-Unit Assessment
Unit 8 Lesson 11: What are Percent Squares
sequence.target: I can recognize perfect-square expressions written in different forms. I can recognize quadratic equations that have a perfect-square expression and solve the equations.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 12: Completing the Square (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can explain what it means to “complete the square” and describe how to do it. I can solve quadratic equations by completing the square and finding square roots.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 13: Completing the Square (Part 2)
sequence.target: When given a quadratic equation in which the coefficient of the squared term is 1, I can solve it by completing the square.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 14: Completing the Square (Part 3)
sequence.target: I can complete the square for quadratic expressions of the form ax^2+bx+c, where a is not 1, and explain the process. I can solve quadratic equations in which the squared term coefficient is not 1 by completing the square.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 15: Quadratic Equations with Irrational Solutions + Section C Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can use the radical and “plus-minus” symbols to represent solutions to quadratic equations. I know why the plus-minus symbol is used when solving quadratic equations by finding square roots.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 16: The Quadratic Formula
sequence.target: I can use the quadratic formula to solve quadratic equations. I know some methods for solving quadratic equations can be more convenient than others.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 17: Applying the Quadratic Formula (Part 1)
sequence.target: I can use the quadratic formula to solve an equation and interpret the solutions in terms of a situation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 18: Applying the Quadratic Formula (Part 2)
sequence.target: I can identify common errors when using the quadratic formula. I know some ways to tell if a number is a solution to a quadratic equation.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 19: Deriving the Quadratic Formula
sequence.target: I can explain the steps and complete some missing steps for deriving the quadratic formula. I know how the quadratic formula is related to the process of completing the square for a quadratic equation ax^2+bx+c=0.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 20: Rational and Irrational Solutions
sequence.target: I can explain why adding a rational number and an irrational number produces an irrational number. I can explain why multiplying a rational number (except 0) and an irrational number produces an irrational number. I can explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 21: Sums and Products of Rational and Irrational Numbers + Section D Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can explain why adding a rational number and an irrational number produces an irrational number. I can explain why multiplying a rational number (except 0) and an irrational number produces an irrational number. I can explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 22: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Vertex Form
sequence.target: I can identify the vertex of the graph of a quadratic function when the expression that defines it is written in vertex form. I know the meaning of the term “vertex form” and can recognize examples of quadratic expressions written in this form. When given a quadratic expression in standard form, I can rewrite it in vertex form.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 23: Using Quadratic Expressions in Vertex Form to Solve Problems + Section E Checkpoint
sequence.target: I can find the maximum or minimum of a function by writing, in vertex form, the quadratic expression that defines it. When given a quadratic function in vertex form, I can explain why the vertex is a maximum or minimum.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Lesson 24: Using Quadratic Equations to Model Situations and Solve Problems
sequence.target: I can interpret information about a quadratic function given its equation or a graph. I can rewrite quadratic functions in different but equivalent forms of my choosing and use that form to solve problems. In situations modeled by quadratic functions, I can decide which form to use depending on the questions being asked.

sequence.district_title: Unit 8 Review
Unit 8 End of Unit Assessment
